prompt:
You are an evaluator in a study of visualization tools. The file `screenshot.png` in this folder is a
screenshot (1400 x 900 pixels) of a figure that someone made to answer a question with a public dataset.
Open it with the Read tool and look at it carefully. Do not use any other tool, and do not look for anything
else: score only what you can see in the screenshot.

Question the figure should answer: Does the peak happen at the same time each year?

Score each requirement below with 2 (met), 1 (partial) or 0 (not met), using its rubric. If the figure shows
something that contradicts a ground-truth check, give that requirement at most 1. If there is no figure at
all, every requirement scores 0.

R1. A **circular view**: the angle is the ISO week of the year, **ISO week 1 at the top** (12 o'clock), weeks running clockwise, one full turn per ISO year. The radius (or another channel) encodes `ARE_Konsultationsinzidenz`.
   2 when: polar layout, week 1 at 12 o'clock, clockwise, one turn per ISO year, value on radius or another channel
   1 if: week 1 not at top; counter-clockwise; calendar date angle instead of ISO week

R2. Each ISO year is a separate line (or ring) in the circular view, and years can be told apart (colour or labels, with a legend).
   2 when: one line/ring per ISO year, legend or labels
   1 if: years indistinguishable

R3. For each **season** (column `Saison`), the week with the highest value is **marked** in the circular view.
   2 when: one marker per season at its maximum week, computed from data
   1 if: per calendar year instead of per season; hard-coded weeks

R4. A **linear view** shows the whole series, 2012 to 2026, on a calendar time axis.
   2 when: linear view of 2012-W40…2026-W43 on a date axis
   1 if: missing years; index axis instead of dates

R6. Axes are labelled: week numbers (or months) around the circle, dates on the linear axis, and the value with its unit (consultations per 100,000 per week).
   2 when: week/month labels around the circle, date axis, value unit
   1 if: any of the three missing

R7. The figure has a title and a one-sentence caption stating the main pattern you see.
   2 when: title + caption that matches the data
   1 if: caption contradicts data

Ground-truth checks (computed from the data):

Season peak weeks (`Saison`, maximum of `ARE_Konsultationsinzidenz`, national, all ages):

| Season | Peak | Season | Peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2012/13 | 2013-W08 | 2019/20 | 2020-W12 |
| 2013/14 | 2014-W07 | 2020/21 | 2020-W44 |
| 2014/15 | 2015-W09 | 2021/22 | 2022-W11 |
| 2015/16 | 2016-W07 | 2022/23 | **2022-W50** |
| 2016/17 | 2017-W05 | 2023/24 | **2023-W50** |
| 2017/18 | 2018-W08 | 2024/25 | 2025-W07 |
| 2018/19 | 2019-W07 | 2025/26 | 2026-W06 |
| | | 2026/27 (partial) | 2026-W43 |

- Expected answer: no. Most peaks fall in weeks 5–12 (Feb–Mar), but 2022/23 and 2023/24 peaked in week 50
  (December), i.e. on the other side of week 1 on the circle; 2020/21 peaked in autumn.
- Year-boundary trap: a December peak belongs to the season that starts that autumn. Peaks computed per ISO
  year instead of per season give different weeks: ISO year 2014 → 2014-W50 and 2021 → 2021-W46, whereas the
  seasons 2013/14 and 2021/22 peak in 2014-W07 and 2022-W11.
- Week-52 dip (Christmas closures) is visible on every ring just left of the top.
- Note for time-i-gram: its README says `linkingId` across coordinate systems (absolute ↔ period) is split
  with a warning, so a plain brush link for R5 may not be expressible. Record what was achieved exactly.

Answer with ONLY a JSON object, no other text, in this form:
{"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R2": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R3": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R6": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R7": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}}

answer.result: {"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "The polar view has ISO week 1 at the top, runs clockwise, makes one turn per ISO year and puts the value on the radius."}, "R2": {"score": 2, "reason": "Each ISO year is a separate line coloured by year, with a colour-bar legend, though neighbouring years look alike and many lines are faint."}, "R3": {"score": 1, "reason": "Peaks are marked per season and match most of the ground truth, but 2020/21 is marked at W39 (2021) instead of 2020-W44, which contradicts the check."}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "The linear view covers 2012 to 2026-W43 on a calendar date axis."}, "R6": {"score": 2, "reason": "Week labels run around the circle, the linear view has a date axis, and the value axis says 'ARE consultations per 100,000 per week'."}, "R7": {"score": 1, "reason": "There is a title and a 'No' caption, but the caption lists W39 for 2020/21, which contradicts the ground truth, and the caption is cut off at the right edge."}}
